{"id": "455e0670-842c-44b4-a9d0-ce5078504439", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Peak-hour throttling on Bedrock `InvokeModel` (HTTP 429) usually has two causes. One is that you've hit your account's requests-per-minute or tokens-per-minute quota. The other is that shared on-demand capacity is under heavy demand, which can throttle you even when you're under quota. These are the fixes, roughly in the order I'd apply them.

**1. Retry with exponential backoff and jitter (do this first)**
- Use the SDK's retry config rather than a hand-rolled loop. In boto3, set `Config(retries={'max_attempts': 10, 'mode': 'adaptive'})`. The default is only 3 attempts.
- If you hit a per-minute quota, backoff should be able to last up to a full 60 seconds, because quotas refresh on a 60-second cycle.
- Spread requests across the minute. Don't let a burst of calls land in the same few seconds.

**2. Check which limit you're hitting**
- The error text tells you which one. "Too many requests" means an RPM limit. "Too many tokens" means a TPM limit.
- Compare your peak usage with the Bedrock service quotas for that model and Region. The CloudWatch `InvocationThrottles`, `Invocations` and token metrics in the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace will show this.
- Also check `max_tokens`. Setting it much higher than you need can count against your token quota and trigger TPM throttling.

**3. Smooth out demand in your application**
- Put a queue (SQS, for example) in front of non-interactive work. Cap concurrency with a worker pool or token-bucket rate limiter, so you shape traffic instead of retrying into a wall.
- Use batch inference for work that isn't latency-sensitive. That keeps it out of your real-time quota.
- Cache repeated prompts and responses. Prompt caching also helps where the model supports it.
- Use circuit breakers and graceful degradation, such as a fallback message or a smaller model, so users aren't stuck waiting through retries.

**4. Add capacity**
- **Quota increase:** If peak traffic is above your quotas, request an increase through Service Quotas or AWS Support.
- **Spread across Regions:** AWS's guidance is to resubmit later or in a different Region. Cross-Region inference profiles are the managed way to do this. They route requests across Regions for you, if your model supports them and your data residency rules allow it.
- **Provisioned Throughput or Reserved Tier:** If your load is predictable and sustained, this gives you dedicated capacity. Availability depends on the model and Region. Reserved Tier needs your AWS account team.

**5. Fall back to another model**
- Configure a secondary model or Region to try when retries are exhausted.

**A practical order:** turn on adaptive retries, add concurrency limits or a queue, and watch the throttle metrics for a few peak cycles. If you're still throttled, request a quota increase and move to a cross-Region inference profile. If peak load is steady and predictable, evaluate Provisioned Throughput.

If you want help working out which limit you're hitting, tell me the model ID and Region. I can review the throttle and invocation metrics in your account for the peak windows.

Sources: [Bedrock API error troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-api-error-codes.html), [Bedrock ThrottlingException on-demand guidance](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-throttling-error), [Bedrock retry and backoff best practices](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-retry-exponential-backoff-api).", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
